To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
scrapie agent strains can be distinguished by the pattern of vacuolation they produce in the brains of infected mice.

the degree of vacuolar damage to the brain and its distribution in different regions is different for each of the 5 strains of scrapie that we used as intracranial inocula, and that these differences can be used to identify each agent with a high degree of reliability, using either of the two mouse strains.

the distribution of grey matter vacolation in the brains of mice infected with different scrapie strains is different for each strain and that this difference is sufficient to distinguish between different scrapie agents.
